WARNING: These are PROPOSALS, not accepted principles. Nothing in this file is part of the SRF principle catalogs. Do not cite an entry here as an established principle, and do not use this file as a source when assessing a document. Whitepaper assessment prompt v2.2 no longer asks users to file candidates. The accepted catalogs are https://aisharedresponsibility.com/data/security-principles.json and https://aisharedresponsibility.com/data/ai-agentic-principles.json.
description: Maintainer review queue for candidate principles. A Novel or Extended finding may land here when a catalog maintainer triages it. Whitepaper assessment prompt v2.2 no longer asks users to file candidates. This is the one file under /data/ that is hand-maintained rather than generated.

lifecycle.proposed: Surfaced by an assessment. No triage done yet.
lifecycle.triaged: Checked against both catalogs and their related links. closest_existing and proposed_disposition are filled in. Not yet decided.
lifecycle.accepted: Judged a genuine addition. incorporated_into records the source file it was written to; the generator then rebuilds the catalog from that source.
lifecycle.extended: Judged a sharpening of an existing entry rather than a new principle. The existing entry may be reworded; no new id is created.
lifecycle.rejected: Judged a duplicate, out of scope, or unsupported. disposition_note records why, so the same candidate is not re-proposed.
lifecycle.deferred: Plausible but blocked, usually pending an OpenCRE check or a source of sufficient evidentiary weight.

evidentiary_tiers.published-standard: A published standard or special publication from a recognized body. Highest weight.
evidentiary_tiers.published-framework: A published framework, guide, or control matrix from an established organization.
evidentiary_tiers.preprint: A preprint or unreviewed paper. Weakest tier. A preprint alone does not justify catalog addition; it can justify watching for corroboration.
evidentiary_tiers.practitioner-report: Vendor or practitioner reporting, including incident write-ups.

incorporation_rules.classic: Additions to security-principles.json are made by editing security_principles_reference.oscal.json. Reserved for settled engineering axioms; contemporary AI-specific findings do not belong there.
incorporation_rules.agentic: Additions to ai-agentic-principles.json are made by editing agentic-ai-security/agentic-security.md. A principle cannot be added without adding its source document to the source table, because the catalog records what specific published papers assert. The generator's CURATION table must be updated in the same change or the build fails.
incorporation_rules.after_editing: Run python3 build/generate_principle_catalogs.py, then commit the regenerated JSON with the source edit.

Calibrates testing depth to system maturity, not to hazardous capability class.

candidates.disposition_note: Incorporated 1 Sep 2026 as hazardous-capability-eval-is-a-release-gate in section red-teaming, citing NIST-218A and FMF-CYBER. candidates.statement: A security boundary is established for tool-initiated callback events, where an external server pushes unsolicited context or events back to the model or host, rather than only for host-initiated calls outward.

surfaced_by.method: whitepaper-assessment prompt v1.0

closest_existing.note: Generic requirement to validate at every boundary crossed. Does not name inbound server-initiated events as a boundary.
Treats outbound communication as one leg of the trifecta. Says nothing about inbound push.

Rejects containers as an MCP boundary without addressing which directions of traffic that boundary must mediate.

candidates.disposition_note: The strongest of the four on novelty. Every nearby entry assumes the host initiates and the tool responds; none address a server pushing unsolicited events back. Blocked on evidentiary weight: a preprint alone does not justify catalog addition under the tiering rules. Watch for corroboration in a published MCP security guide, then accept.

candidates.statement: Security invariants are defined for runtime tool schema updates and dynamic capability discovery, so a tool changing its declared interface mid-session is treated as a change requiring revalidation rather than as normal operation.

source.label: arXiv:2503.23278v3

surfaced_by.method: whitepaper-assessment prompt v1.0

closest_existing.note: Pins and checksums approved server and tool versions to block a silent malicious upgrade. Addresses version substitution between sessions, not schema mutation within one.

candidates.disposition_note: Sits between Extended and Novel. pinned-checksum-verified-versions covers the between-sessions case and explicit-per-capability-grants covers grant breadth, but neither covers a tool mutating its schema mid-session.
